newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian Metals-Aluminium seen enlivening dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian Metals-Aluminium seen enlivening dull trade.

text.p: Aluminium is expected to put some life into an otherwise dull non-ferrous metals trade on demand spurred by low domestic prices, traders said on Wednesday.
They said domestic aluminium prices were lower at 7,800 rupees per quintal (100 kg) compared to the imported metal cost at 9,500 rupees.
"Lower domestic prices have certainly pushed up demand for aluminium," said Bombay Metal Exchange president Sharad Parikh.
Analysts said prices of imported aluminium were higher because of a firm trend on the London Metal Exchange, (LME) helped by upbeat economies of the United States and Japan.
"Aluminium prices on LME are expected to move upwards, which will greatly benefit the Indian aluminium industry," said a senior official of Hindalco Ltd, India's premier private sector company.
Demand for aluminium from the domestic power sector and packaging industries is expected to grow faster than before.
Analysts said they would expect domestic demand to grow at 5.5 percent in 1997/98 (April/March) against 4.5 percent in the previous year.
On the Bombay metals market, aluminium remained steady at 7,800 rupees per quintal in the week to Wednesday.
"Local producers have not raised their prices nor are likely to do so because of a firm trend on LME," Parikh said.
On Wednesday, Hindalco chairman Kumar Mangalam Birla told the company's annual meeting in Bombay that he saw a bright future ahead for the company.

"With our well-defined business strategy, the completion of the ongoing capital expenditure programme and the utilisation of enhanced capacities and facilities, the outlook for the future is exceedingly bright," he said.
All other base metals were quiet on the local non-ferrous metals market.
Copper lost 300 rupees to 13,200 rupees per quintal reflecting the weak LME trend.

A copper smelter with an annual capacity of 100,000 tonnes had been ordered to close because of the reported leakage of a toxic gas. Company officials said last week they hoped to restart the smelter shortly.
Zinc lead and tin were steady at 8,400 rupees, 4,200 rupees, 29,200 rupees per quintal.
Nickel lost 200 rupees to 34,100 rupees per quintal.
